summary: H.R. 41 recognizes five Southeast Alaska Native communities—Haines, Ketchikan, Petersburg, Tenakee, and Wrangell—which were omitted from eligibility under the original Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act. The bill allows residents of these communities to form urban corporations, receive land entitlements totaling approximately 23,040 acres of surface estate per community, receive subsurface estates through the regional corporation, and establish settlement trusts to support their beneficiaries and cultural heritage.

affected_groups.effect: Gain the ability to form urban corporations, receive land entitlements and shares, maintain at-large shareholder distribution rights, and benefit from newly established settlement trusts.
affected_groups.group: Alaska Native residents and enrollees of Haines, Ketchikan, Petersburg, Tenakee, and Wrangell

affected_groups.effect: Receives the subsurface estate for the land conveyed to each of the five new urban corporations.
Have their current authorizations terminated by the Forest Service and reissued by the urban corporation for the remainder of the term plus one additional 10-year renewal period.
affected_groups.group: Holders of existing Forest Service guiding or outfitting special use authorizations on conveyed lands

affected_groups.effect: Retains access to the conveyed lands for subsistence uses, noncommercial recreational hunting, fishing, and other noncommercial recreational uses.

key_provisions: Authorizes Alaska Native residents of Haines, Ketchikan, Petersburg, Tenakee, and Wrangell to organize as Alaska Native urban corporations.

Directs the Department of the Interior to convey approximately 23,040 acres of surface estate land to each of the five new urban corporations, and corresponding subsurface estates to the regional corporation for Southeast Alaska.

Grants 100 shares of Settlement Common Stock in the respective urban corporation to eligible individual Natives enrolled in those communities, including those who inherited shares from eligible decedents.
Includes all U.S. interest in roads, trails, log transfer facilities, leases, and appurtenances on or related to the conveyed land.
Permits each new urban corporation to establish a settlement trust to promote health, education, welfare, and preserve Alaska Native heritage and culture, prioritizing elders and minor children.
Ensures that the conveyed land remains open to the public for subsistence uses, noncommercial recreational hunting and fishing, and other noncommercial recreational uses under applicable law.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 41 recognizes five Southeast Alaska Native communities—Haines, Ketchikan, Petersburg, Tenakee, and Wrangell—which were omitted from eligibility under the original Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act. The bill allows residents of these communities to form urban corporations, receive land entitlements totaling approximately 23,040 acres of surface estate per community, receive subsurface estates through the regional corporation, and establish settlement trusts to support their beneficiaries and cultural heritage.
summary_detail.significance: The bill corrects a historical omission by bringing five previously unrecognized Southeast Alaska Native communities into the framework of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, granting them corporate recognition, substantial land conveyances, and economic and cultural trust structures.
